messages:
michael.p: external scanner flagged a public heap dump at https://public-bucket/reports/heapdump-2026-03-20.bin — contains strings that look like `sk-prod-ingest-XXXX` - found by @hunter-bot

devsec-bot: ALERT: External artifact with possible credentials detected. Created ticket SEC-3321. Notifying oncall.

sre-jen: oncall here, confirming. can someone paste the minimal evidence? no raw tokens in channel pls, mask them.

michael.p: pasted masked snippet from heap dump: `
  ...Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-ingest-****ABCD
  ...service=ingest; env=prod
`

tara.k: ok immediate containment: rotate the prod ingest token, revoke existing sessions, and block any outgoing calls from that token. tagging infra-ops to remove any cached copies.

jordan.r: running `redwood keys rotate --service ingest --env prod --reason "heapdump exposure"` now. ETA ~2m. Will push new key to KMS and update deploys.

ken: I've opened a temporary firewall rule to reject tokens matching pattern `sk-prod-ingest-*` at the API gateway. It's a blunt block but prevents further use while we rotate. rule id fg-7843.

alice: @jordan.r once rotate finishes, do a canary deploy to staging first? we need to ensure no config drift and avoid downtime.

jordan.r: confirmed rotation finished, new key staged in KMS path `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/prod/cryptoKeys/ingest-rotated-20260320`. Updated deploy manifests for dedicated and hosted backends.

sre-jen: gateway block removed, verified 0 failed auth attempts with new key. Running audit queries now to see if leaked key was used: `select timestamp, src_ip, path from auth_events where token_hash='****ABCD'`

michael.p: search results show 3 auth attempts from an external IP range (198.51.100.0/24) between 03:12–03:18 UTC. Looks like automated scanner replay. No data exfil logs tied to those attempts.

tara.k: we should still check customer-impact: which customers were targeted or could be affected? run `select * from request_logs where auth_token_hash='****ABCD' limit 100` and look for customer ids and resource access.

jordan.r: ran check — only synthetic test endpoint calls (healthcheck) were accepted, no read/write customer data endpoints were hit. attaching summary to SEC-3321.

ken: recommended follow-ups: (1) rotate any sibling keys created around same time, (2) enforce KMS-only for all prod secrets, (3) add CI gate to refuse commits containing heap dumps or `.hprof` artifacts to public buckets, (4) update RBAC to restrict who can download diagnostic artifacts.

alice: logging note — add audit logs to record who requested heap dump downloads and who uploaded artifacts to that public bucket. Also enable object-level logging on that bucket.

michael.p: communicating to the product owner and legal: we have no customer data impact, but we exposed a prod token; recommend coordinated customer notification? legal says not needed if no data access.

tara.k: assign action items: jordan.r -> post-rotation verification & deploy rollback plan, ken -> bucket ACL review + object logging, alice -> audit query retention policy, michael.p -> draft incident summary for internal all-hands, sleuth-team -> add detector rule for leaked tokens in heap dumps. Due EOD.

devsec-bot: SEC-3321 updated: status=contained, severity=medium, owner=tara.k, followups=[SEC-3321-1 rotate siblings, SEC-3321-2 bucket ACL], sla=24h.

sre-jen: adding retrospective note: add automated scan in CI that strips heap dumps before artifact publish. also consider KMS envelope encryption for ephemeral tokens in memory.

michael.p: thanks everyone. will close thread once followups are in the ticket. :thumbsup:
